newsitem.title: UK: UK Interoute Telecoms joins AIM with sights on EU.
newsitem.headline: UK Interoute Telecoms joins AIM with sights on EU.

text.p: Interoute Telecommunications said on Friday its planned float on London's Alternative Investment Market at a placing price of 150 pence per share valued the UK-based wholesale telephony service firm at 50 million stg.
Interoute said it was positioning itself to take advantage of the liberalisation of European telecoms markets around 1998.

The telecommunications operator makes its money as an intermediary between public telephone operators and telecommunications companies in Europe and the U.S. by trading in the differentials arising from individual companies' cost and pricing structures.

"These rates give a low-cost base for the worldwide delivery of traffic, an essential prerequisite for successfully competing in Europe, and provide the foundation for a successful international telecommunications business," it said.
Trading in the shares is expected to start on October 3.

In a prospectus, the firm said turnover in the year to May 1998 was expected to rise to 58.0 million stg from 13.1 million the previous year. From a projected loss of 1.5 million stg in 1997, a pre-tax profit of four million is projected for 1998.
Interoute has established businesses in France and Switzerland and installed nodes in Germany and the Netherlands.

"The Directors view the retail network in Europe as the group's primary source of future growth as, following liberalisation in Europe, the addressable market is expected to expand rapidly," it added in a statement.
John East & Partners Limited is the nominated adviser and HSBC James Capel is the nominated broker to Interoute and underwriter of the placing.
The company is placing about 7.36 million ordinary shares.
